sections.h2: What is the quickest way to sell a house in Centerville, Ohio?
sections.html:
A direct cash sale is the quickest path in Centerville, while a retail listing usually earns the stronger price. Centerville is a core suburb of the Dayton area, so a house in good order can attract buyers on the open market.

  • List with an agent: the better route for a maintained house in a desirable school zone. Plan for staging, showings, and a buyer's inspection.
  • Sell as-is for cash: sensible when the house needs a roof, mechanicals, or cosmetic work you would rather not fund before selling.
  • Sell privately: possible if you already have a buyer, such as a relative or neighbor. A written contract and a title company still protect both sides.

The Census Bureau shows 85.3% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so most sellers here have been in place for some time and know the house well.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers show for Centerville homes?
sections.html:
Centerville skews older and owner-occupied. In the 2020 census the median age was 48.8, and 29.5% of residents were 65 or older, with 70.4% of occupied homes lived in by their owners. The Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate of 25,194 residents is 4.2% above its 2020 base.

sections.h2: How old is Centerville, and what does that mean for a house here?
sections.html:
Centerville was first surveyed in February 1796, recognized by the state in 1803, platted in 1805, and incorporated as a town in 1830. It became a city on December 2, 1968. The post office changed the spelling from Centreville to Centerville in 1900.

The city is known for early stone houses cut from local limestone. Wikipedia reports nearly 100 stone buildings lined local streets in the nineteenth century, many still stand, and the city has the largest collection of early stone houses in Ohio, with a number on the National Register of Historic Places. If you own a house in the historic core around the Heart of Centerville, ask the city whether architectural review applies to exterior changes before you promise a buyer a renovation.

Away from the old center, most of the housing came with suburban growth. School enrollment rose past 6,800 students by 1969, and Centerville High School moved to its current campus in 1973, which gives a sense of when much of the city filled in.

sections.h2: How is a Centerville sale recorded in Montgomery County?
sections.html:
A Centerville house sale is recorded by the Montgomery County Recorder after the deed passes through the Auditor's Deed Transfer Department. A small part of the city lies in Greene County, so check which county holds your parcel before you start.

According to the Recorder's FAQ, a deed must show the buyer and seller names, the legal description, the seller's signature, and a notary block, and it needs the Auditor's transfer or no-transfer stamp. Documents are recorded the same business day they are received, once the Auditor has transferred them. Documents that need a No Transfer stamp, such as transfer on death designations and easements, are mailed or walked through the Auditor's department rather than filed electronically. Ask the Recorder for the current fee schedule before you file.

  • Revised Code 319.202 has the buyer file a value statement with the auditor, and the seller pays the conveyance fee.
  • The deed you received when you bought is not replaced when you pay off a mortgage. The lender files a release, which you can view on the county's online records search.
  • Montgomery County has roughly 230,000 parcels, so use the parcel number from your tax bill on every form.

sections.h2: How do I contest my Centerville property value?
sections.html:
Property owners in Montgomery County file a complaint with the Board of Revision between January 1 and March 31, and the form must state the value you want and why. The statewide statute, Revised Code 5715.19, also allows a later filing date when first-half collection closes after March 31.

The complainant carries the burden of proof. Evidence the board accepts includes a sale of the property in the last three years, a recent independent appraisal, recent sales of similar nearby homes, a realtor's comparative market analysis, and itemized repair estimates. It does not accept the county's assessed values of other properties, descriptions of how neighbors keep up their yards, or complaints about the tax rate.

Hearings for tax year 2025 were held by video or phone and lasted 10 to 20 minutes per property. The board mails its decision within 90 days, and an appeal goes to the Ohio Board of Tax Appeals or the Court of Common Pleas within 30 days. A changed value stays in effect until the next countywide update, which comes every three years unless the property is rebuilt or damaged.

sections.h2: What must a Centerville seller disclose?
sections.html:
Revised Code 5302.30 requires the seller of a one to four unit home to complete the state disclosure form and deliver it to the buyer. It asks about the water supply, the sewer or septic system, the roof, foundation, walls and floors, and known hazards such as lead paint or radon.

The statute carves out transfers by a fiduciary in an estate, transfers between spouses or to a lineal relative, and a sale by an heir who did not live in the home in the preceding year. If a buyer gets the form after signing, the buyer has three business days to rescind, and no later than the earlier of 30 days after acceptance or closing. Disclose what you know about the house; Centerville is subject to tornadoes, floods, and severe storms, so tell buyers about any past storm or water damage.

sections.h2: Which schools, hospitals, and amenities draw buyers to Centerville?
sections.html:
The Centerville City School District serves the city with two primary schools, six elementary schools, three middle schools, and Centerville High School, plus an alternative high school. The Washington-Centerville Public Library holds more than 380,000 items.

Miami Valley Hospital South opened in 2007 as an outpatient facility with an emergency department and grew into a full-service hospital by 2013 with 60 beds on a campus next to Interstate 675. It is the largest employer in the city according to Wikipedia, which also lists retail and health care as the biggest job categories. The city runs on a city manager form of government with a seven-member council elected at large, and the downtown Town Hall Theatre dates to 1908. The Census puts 2022 retail sales per resident at $44,802.

faqs.q: Does Centerville sit in one county?
faqs.a: Mostly in Montgomery County, with a small portion in Greene County. Check the county named on your tax bill and deed. That county's auditor, treasurer, and recorder handle your sale paperwork.

faqs.q: Do I need an architectural review to sell a historic stone house in Centerville?
faqs.a: Ask the city's planning and zoning office whether your address is in a historic area with review rules before you sell or renovate. Check this before you promise a buyer any exterior changes.

faqs.q: Who pays the conveyance fee when I sell in Centerville?
faqs.a: The seller. Revised Code 319.202 says the grantor pays it, and the auditor endorses the deed after the buyer files the statement of value. Your closing statement will show the exact figure.

faqs.q: When can I file a value complaint in Montgomery County?
faqs.a: Between January 1 and March 31 each year, using the county's complaint form. Bring evidence of market value, such as a recent sale, an appraisal, or repair estimates, and submit it to the evidence portal at least 10 days before the hearing.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited house in Centerville without the disclosure form?
faqs.a: Often yes. Revised Code 5302.30 excludes sales by an estate fiduciary, and a transfer by an heir who did not live in the home for the prior year. If you lived there, complete the form. A title company or attorney can confirm which applies to you.
